experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded cove for a refreshing swim.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most beautiful sea caves, accessible only by water. A guided kayak tour takes you through hidden grottos and arches along the golden coastline, offering a unique perspective of the Algarve's dramatic geology.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience
experiences.description: Visit a local winery in the Lagoa wine region, the heart of Algarve viticulture, for a guided tasting of regional wines including Arinto and Negra Mole varieties. Pair your wines with a traditional Cataplana seafood stew prepared by a local chef.

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat Tour
experiences.description: Cruise through the stunning Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park spanning 60km of coastline. Discover barrier islands, flamingo colonies, and secluded barrier beaches only accessible by boat, with stops for swimming and snorkeling in calm lagoon waters.

experiences.name: Silves Castle & Old Town Food Walk
experiences.description: Explore the Moorish red sandstone castle of Silves, the ancient Algarve capital, followed by a guided food walk through the historic old town. Sample local specialties including carob products, medronho brandy, almond sweets, and fresh orange juice at traditional market stalls.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Boutique Taghostel
hotel.location: Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos, PT (37.1038,-8.6730)

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Take the budget-friendly Eva Bus or Rede Expressos coach from Faro Airport to Lagos (approx. €5-7, ~1.5 hours). Check into Boutique Taghostel on Rua Dr. Faria e Silva. Freshen up and get settled.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack at a nearby 24h mini-market or a kebab/pizza slice shop near the hostel in Lagos old town (under €5)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the Faro–Lagos bus ticket online to save time. The hostel is centrally located in Lagos, a short walk from the bus station. Keep luggage light for easy transit. Exchange some euros before leaving the airport if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy the hostel's common area. Walk to the Lagos Municipal Market (Mercado Municipal) for a cheap, fresh breakfast and to soak in local morning life. Stroll along the old town walls and visit the free Igreja de Santa Maria church.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia Beach (a 20-minute walk or short bus ride, free entry) — one of the longest and least crowded beaches near Lagos. Swim, relax, and enjoy the September sun with fewer tourists than peak summer. Bring snacks from the market to save money.
day_by_day.evening: Walk back into Lagos old town. Explore the lively Rua 25 de Abril for bar-hopping. Visit a local tasca (tavern) for a budget dinner. Try the famous Lagos nightlife scene — many bars offer happy hour deals.

meals.breakfast: Fresh pastries and coffee at Mercado Municipal Lagos (€2-3)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks from the market or a simple sandwich from a padaria (bakery) near the beach (€3-5)
meals.dinner: Tasca do Chico or similar local tasca — prato do dia (dish of the day) with bread, wine, and dessert (€8-12)

day_by_day.notes: September is ideal — warm water, fewer crowds, and lower prices than July/August. Bring sunscreen and a reusable water bottle. The hostel may offer free maps of the area.

day_by_day.morning: Take a short walk or local bus to Praia Dona Ana — one of the most scenic beaches in the Algarve with dramatic golden cliffs. Arrive early to claim a good spot. Explore the cliff-top walking path for stunning views and free photography opportunities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the coastal cliff path from Dona Ana toward Praia do Camilo (about 15 minutes on foot). Descend the wooden staircase to this intimate, sheltered beach. Continue the cliff walk toward Ponta da Piedade — a spectacular free natural landmark with sea caves and rock arches. Peer down from the clifftops for free (boat tours are optional, ~€15 if budget allows).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos town center. Visit a local supermarket (Lidl or Pingo Doce) to pick up a bottle of affordable Algarve wine (€3-5). Enjoy a sunset picnic on the town's waterfront promenade along the Arade River esplanade.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast if included, or a pastel de nata and galão coffee at a local café (€2-3)
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach — grab a baguette, local cheese, and fruit from a nearby mini-market (€4-6)
meals.dinner: O Camilo restaurant near Ponta da Piedade for fresh grilled fish (look for the prato do dia, €10-13) or cook a simple meal at the hostel kitchen

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy shoes for the cliff walk — some paths are uneven. The walk from Dona Ana to Ponta da Piedade is approximately 2km and takes about 45 minutes at a leisurely pace. Sunset from Ponta da Piedade is spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local Rede Expressos or Eva Bus to Sagres (approx. €4-5 each way, ~45 minutes from Lagos). Visit the impressive Fortaleza de Sagres (€3 entry) — a 15th-century fortress at the southwestern tip of Europe with dramatic ocean views and historical significance as the base of Henry the Navigator.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Cabo de São Vicente (about 6km from Sagres, or take a taxi for ~€8-10 one way) — the most southwestern point of continental Europe. The lighthouse and cliffs are breathtaking and free to visit from the outside. Browse the small artisan market at the cape for souvenirs. Return to Sagres and relax at Praia do Martinhal or Praia de Sagres.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by bus. Have dinner in Lagos old town. Friday evenings are lively — enjoy the atmosphere of the pedestrian streets.

meals.breakfast: Quick coffee and toast at the hostel or a café near the bus station before departure (€2-3)
meals.lunch: A Sagres local café or snack bar near the fortress — try a bifana (pork sandwich) or soup (€4-7)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega in Lagos or similar — grilled sardines or bacalhau (codfish) with local wine (€10-14)

day_by_day.notes: Check the bus schedule in advance as Sagres buses run limited times. The wind at Cabo de São Vicente can be very strong — bring a light jacket. The lighthouse gift shop sells affordable local honey and ceramics.

day_by_day.morning: Take a bus or walk to Praia da Luz (about 6km west of Lagos, local bus ~€1.50). This charming village beach is quieter than Lagos beaches and has a lovely promenade. Swim and relax in the morning calm. Explore the small village center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the coastal trail from Praia da Luz toward Burgau (approximately 5km, 1.5 hours) along dramatic clifftops. Descend into the tiny fishing village of Burgau and enjoy its small beach. This is a hidden gem with far fewer tourists. Return to Lagos by local bus from Burgau (check schedule, ~€2).
day_by_day.evening: Saturday night in Lagos — the town comes alive. Visit the Mercado de Levante night market if running (seasonal). Enjoy a cheap beer or glass of local wine at one of the outdoor bars on Rua Cândido dos Reis. Try a late dinner at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hostel kitchen or a padaria near the hostel — toast, eggs, and coffee (€3-4)
meals.lunch: A simple meal at a café in Burgau village — fresh fish of the day or a sandwich (€7-10)
meals.dinner: Casinha do Petisco in Lagos or similar — petiscos (Portuguese tapas) shared between travelers from the hostel (€8-12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Luz to Burgau coastal walk is moderately easy but bring water and sun protection. Saturday markets in Lagos old town are worth a browse in the morning before heading out. Great opportunity to meet fellow hostel travelers for the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning — sleep in or enjoy the hostel common area. Visit the Lagos Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos) — the only museum of its kind in Europe, very affordable entry (~€3). Then explore the Museu Municipal Dr. José Formosinho for local history and artifacts (~€2).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a local bus to Meia Praia for a relaxed Sunday afternoon beach session. The long sandy beach is perfect for a long walk, swimming, and people-watching. Alternatively, rent a kayak or SUP board from a local beach rental (€10-15/hour) for some active fun.
day_by_day.evening: Sunday evening stroll through Lagos old town. Visit the weekly local artisan market if available. Cook a communal dinner at the hostel with ingredients from the supermarket — a great way to bond with fellow travelers and save money.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or a leisurely café brunch in the old town — eggs, toast, juice (€4-6)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Meia Praia — grilled chicken piri-piri or a fresh salad (€7-10)
meals.dinner: Self-cooked hostel meal — pasta with local chorizo, vegetables, and a bottle of Algarve wine from Lidl (€4-6 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Sunday is a good day to recharge. Many restaurants offer a Sunday special menu. The hostel kitchen is a great resource — check if it's available for guest use. Stock up on groceries at Pingo Doce or Lidl for the week to save on meal costs.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early bus to Portimão (Eva Bus, ~€3, 30 minutes). Walk across the bridge to Ferragudo — a picturesque fishing village with a castle, colorful boats, and a lovely beach (Praia Grande de Ferragudo). Explore the village streets and the Castelo de São João do Arade (exterior free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia da Rocha in Portimão — one of the most famous beaches in the Algarve with impressive rock formations. Walk the beach promenade and explore the sea caves accessible on foot at low tide. Visit the Portimão Museum (Museu de Portimão) — free on Sunday, €3 other days — housed in a former sardine canning factory.
day_by_day.evening: Have dinner in Portimão before catching the bus back to Lagos. Portimão is famous for its grilled sardines — try the riverside restaurants near the old fishing docks for the best and most affordable options.

meals.breakfast: Quick coffee and pastel de nata at a café near Lagos bus station before departure (€2)
meals.lunch: A simple meal in Ferragudo village — fresh fish soup and bread at a local café (€6-9)
meals.dinner: Riverside sardine restaurant in Portimão — grilled sardines, salad, and local wine (€10-13)

day_by_day.notes: Ferragudo is often overlooked by tourists and is far more authentic than nearby Portimão. The walk across the bridge from Portimão to Ferragudo takes about 15 minutes. Check bus return times to Lagos before heading out.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting day! Take a bus or arrange a shared taxi to Quinta dos Vales winery near Estômbar/Lagoa (approximately 30km east of Lagos). This is one of the most accessible and affordable wineries in the Algarve. Book a basic tasting session in advance (€10-15 for 4-5 wines with light snacks). The estate also has impressive outdoor sculptures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to nearby Lagoa town — the wine capital of the Algarve. Visit the Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa (Lagoa Wine Cooperative) for an affordable tasting of local Algarve wines (€5-8 for a tasting flight). Browse the cooperative's shop for budget-friendly bottles to take home. Explore Lagoa's charming town center.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by bus. Enjoy a relaxed evening — perhaps a wine and cheese night at the hostel with bottles purchased from the cooperative. Share the experience with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Hostel or local café before departure (€2-4)
meals.lunch: Light snacks included with wine tasting, or a simple meal at a café in Lagoa town center (€6-9)
meals.dinner: Hostel kitchen or a local Lagos restaurant — try a bifana sandwich or a simple prato do dia (€6-10)

day_by_day.notes: Book winery visits in advance, especially Quinta dos Vales. Consider sharing a taxi with hostel friends to split costs. The Algarve produces excellent but underrated wines — particularly the local red blends and the Moscatel de Faro dessert wine. Buy a bottle or two at the cooperative for the best prices.

day_by_day.morning: Take a bus to Silves (Eva Bus from Lagos, ~€4, 1 hour with a change in Portimão). Visit the magnificent Castelo de Silves — a well-preserved Moorish castle with panoramic views over the Algarve interior (€2.80 entry). Explore the red sandstone walls and towers. Visit the adjacent Sé Catedral de Silves (small entry fee or free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through Silves old town — one of the most historically rich towns in the Algarve and the former Moorish capital. Visit the Museu Arqueológico de Silves (€2). Stroll along the Arade River waterfront. If time allows, visit a local quinta (farm estate) near Silves for a casual wine or medronho (arbutus berry spirit) tasting.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by bus. Enjoy a quiet evening in the hostel or explore a new restaurant in Lagos you haven't tried yet.

meals.breakfast: Hostel or café near Lagos bus station (€2-3)
meals.lunch: Café Inglês in Silves (near the castle) or a local tasca — cataplana (traditional Algarve seafood stew) if budget allows, or a simpler prato do dia (€8-12)
meals.dinner: A Forja restaurant in Lagos or similar — traditional Portuguese grilled meats with local wine (€10-14)

day_by_day.notes: Silves is a must-visit for history lovers. The town is far less touristy than coastal resorts. September is harvest season in the Algarve — you may see grape and fig harvesting in the countryside around Silves. The bus connection requires a change in Portimão — allow extra time.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the beaches east of Lagos. Take a local bus to Alvor (€2, ~20 minutes). Walk through the charming fishing village of Alvor with its whitewashed houses and Manueline church. Then head to the stunning Alvor Estuary boardwalk — a free wooden walkway through the natural reserve with incredible birdwatching and views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Praia de Alvor — a wide, beautiful beach backed by dunes. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing. The beach is less crowded than Praia da Rocha and has a more natural feel. Walk the dune path toward Meia Praia for a scenic coastal hike.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Visit the local fish market (if still open in the late afternoon) to see the day's catch. Have dinner at a restaurant specializing in fresh seafood near the Lagos waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Hostel or a padaria in Lagos before departure (€2-3)
meals.lunch: A beach snack bar in Alvor or a picnic from the village mini-market (€5-8)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Camilo or a waterfront Lagos restaurant — fresh grilled sea bass or bream with salad and wine (€12-15)

day_by_day.notes: The Alvor Estuary is a protected natural area — stay on the boardwalk and respect the wildlife. Bring binoculars if you have them for birdwatching. Alvor village has a lovely weekly market on Tuesdays — check if there's a local market during your visit.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Tavira — one of the most beautiful towns in the Algarve (take the train from Lagos via Faro, ~2.5 hours, €10-12 one way — book in advance for best prices). Explore Tavira's Roman bridge, castle ruins (free), and the Igreja de Santa Maria do Castelo. Stroll along the Gilão River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the ferry from Tavira to Ilha de Tavira (€1.50 each way) — a stunning barrier island beach with crystal-clear water and a natural park setting. This is one of the most beautiful and unspoiled beaches in the entire Algarve. Swim, relax, and enjoy the natural beauty.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tavira for dinner before catching the train back to Lagos. Tavira has excellent and affordable seafood restaurants. The town is beautifully lit in the evening.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Lagos train station café before departure (€2-3)
meals.lunch: Picnic on Ilha de Tavira — buy supplies in Tavira market before taking the ferry (€5-7)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bica in Tavira or similar — fresh clams (ameijoas) and grilled fish with local wine (€10-14)

day_by_day.notes: This is a long day trip — start early. The train is the most budget-friendly option and the journey through the Algarve countryside is scenic. Ilha de Tavira is a protected natural area — no permanent structures, just pristine beach. Check the last train back to Lagos and plan accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — revisit your favorite beach or try Praia do Porto de Mós (a 30-minute walk from Lagos hostel along the coast path). This is a beautiful, less-crowded beach with dramatic cliffs. Spend the morning swimming and soaking up the last of the Algarve sun.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos for a final afternoon of souvenir shopping in the old town. Visit the local artisan shops on Rua 25 de Abril for affordable ceramics, cork products, and local food items (dried figs, almonds, local wine). Visit the Saturday market if running. Pack any purchases carefully.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Lagos — splurge slightly on a nicer meal to celebrate the trip. Visit a wine bar for a final tasting of Algarve wines. Connect with fellow hostel travelers for a final evening out on the town.

meals.breakfast: A leisurely café breakfast in Lagos old town — full Portuguese breakfast with eggs, presunto, cheese, and coffee (€5-7)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Porto de Mós or a packed lunch (€5-8)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina or similar — a slightly splurge-worthy farewell meal with cataplana, local wine, and dessert (€15-20)

day_by_day.notes: Porto de Mós beach requires a walk down a steep path — wear appropriate footwear. Saturday is the best day for markets and shopping in Lagos. Consider buying a bottle of local Algarve wine or medronho as a souvenir — the cooperative in Lagoa or local supermarkets have the best prices.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Boutique Taghostel (confirm checkout time — typically 11:00). Store luggage at the hostel if needed. Take a final morning walk through Lagos old town — visit the waterfront, the old city walls, and grab a last pastel de nata and coffee at your favorite café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, take the Eva Bus or Rede Expressos from Lagos to Faro Airport (€5-7, ~1.5 hours). Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before your flight for the bus journey and airport check-in. Browse the airport shops for any last-minute Portuguese treats.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days exploring the beaches, wines, and culture of the Algarve!

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and galão coffee at a Lagos café — a perfect farewell to Portugal (€2-3)
meals.lunch: A light meal at the Lagos bus station café or a sandwich to eat on the bus (€4-6)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or café at Faro Airport, or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your bus departure time from Lagos to Faro the evening before. The Lagos bus station is about a 10-minute walk from the hostel. Keep your travel documents, boarding pass, and passport easily accessible. Consider downloading the CP (Comboios de Portugal) and Rede Expressos apps for easy transport booking throughout the trip.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Take the airport shuttle or a pre-booked taxi (~1 hour) to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos. Check in, freshen up, and grab a late-night snack at a nearby 24-hour café or the hostel's common area. Get oriented with a map of Lagos for the days ahead.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night snack at a nearby café or convenience store near the hostel – try a pastel de nata and a light sandwich

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light – only arrival activities. Pre-book your taxi from Faro Airport in advance to avoid waiting. Confirm check-in arrangements with Taghostel as arrival is late night. Pack light for easy transit.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, enjoy breakfast at the hostel or a nearby café. Take a gentle orientation walk through Lagos Old Town – explore the historic city walls, Praça Gil Eanes, and the charming cobblestone streets. Visit the Igreja de Santo António for a glimpse of stunning azulejo tilework.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia, Lagos's longest and most accessible beach (15-minute walk or short taxi). Spend the afternoon swimming, sunbathing, and relaxing on the golden sands. Rent a sun lounger and umbrella for comfort. The calm waters make it ideal for a first beach day.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Lagos marina at sunset. Enjoy dinner at a mid-range restaurant along the waterfront. Explore the lively Rua 25 de Abril bar street for a casual evening drink.

meals.breakfast: Café Ginginha or a local pastelaria near the hostel – coffee, toast, and pastries (~€5–8)
meals.lunch: Beachside snack bar at Meia Praia – grilled fish sandwich and fresh juice (~€10–14)
meals.dinner: O Camilo Restaurant or similar – grilled sea bass or cataplana de marisco with local wine (~€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: September in the Algarve is warm and sunny (avg. 25–28°C) with fewer crowds than peak summer – ideal beach conditions. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and water. Lagos Old Town is very walkable from the hostel.

day_by_day.morning: Take the short bus or taxi to Praia Dona Ana (10 minutes from Lagos). Explore the dramatic golden limestone cliffs and sea stacks. Swim in the crystal-clear turquoise waters. Arrive early to secure a good spot on this popular but stunning beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the coastal cliff path from Praia Dona Ana toward Praia do Camilo and Ponta da Piedade. This 2–3 km scenic trail offers breathtaking views of the Algarve's iconic rock formations. Descend the wooden staircase at Ponta da Piedade to explore the sea arches and grottos up close. Optionally, hire a local fisherman's boat for a 30-minute grotto tour (~€10–15 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos for the evening. Browse the artisan shops and boutiques in the old town. Enjoy a relaxed dinner in the historic center.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria Mota near the hostel – fresh orange juice, croissant, and coffee (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Praia Dona Ana or a packed lunch from a local deli – sandwiches, fruit, and water (~€8–12)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina – traditional Portuguese petiscos (tapas) and a glass of Algarve wine (~€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the cliff path. The path is mostly flat but has some uneven terrain. The Ponta da Piedade boat tours are informal – negotiate directly with the fishermen at the bottom of the stairs. Bring cash.

day_by_day.morning: Book the Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim experience. Depart from Lagos by rental car or organized tour (~45 minutes east). Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear waters. The guided coastal hike reveals hidden coves and spectacular viewpoints before descending to the beach for a swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Marinha coastline independently. Snorkel in the clear waters around the rock formations. Relax on the beach and soak in the scenery. In the late afternoon, drive or take the tour bus back toward Lagos, stopping at Carvoeiro village for a stroll along its picturesque beach promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a quiet evening at the hostel's common area, meeting fellow travelers. Head out for a casual dinner in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or nearby café – yogurt, fruit, toast, and coffee (~€6–9)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snack bar near Praia da Marinha – local cheese, bread, and fruit (~€8–12)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Casinha do Petisco – hearty Portuguese home cooking, try the bacalhau à brás (~€16–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Praia da Marinha is about 45 km east of Lagos. Renting a car for this day gives maximum flexibility (~€35–50/day). Alternatively, book an organized day tour from Lagos that includes transport. The beach has limited facilities – bring water and snacks.

day_by_day.morning: Book the Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience in the Lagoa wine region (~30 minutes east of Lagos). Visit a local winery for a guided tour of the vineyards and wine cellar. Learn about the unique Algarve terroir and the indigenous grape varieties like Negra Mole and Crato Branco.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine experience with a traditional cataplana tasting lunch at the winery – a copper-pot seafood or meat stew paired with local wines. After the experience, explore the charming town of Lagoa briefly before heading back toward Lagos. Stop at a local wine shop to pick up a bottle or two as souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a lighter evening after the indulgent lunch. Take a sunset walk along the Lagos seafront promenade. Have a casual dinner or tapas at a wine bar.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hostel – coffee and pastries (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Included in the Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience – traditional cataplana with wine pairings
meals.dinner: Wine bar dinner – cheese and charcuterie board with a glass of local wine (~€15–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the wine tasting experience in advance, especially on weekends. The cataplana lunch is typically included in the experience package. Designate a driver if renting a car, or arrange transport through the tour operator. This is a highlight experience – don't miss it.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente – the southwestern tip of Europe. Drive or take the bus (~1 hour from Lagos). Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres, a 15th-century fortress perched on the cliffs. Explore the windswept promontory and learn about Portugal's Age of Discovery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive 6 km to Cabo de São Vicente, the most southwestern point of continental Europe. Stand at the edge of the world and watch the Atlantic waves crash against the 75-meter cliffs. Browse the small market stalls selling local crafts and dried herbs. Visit Praia do Beliche, a secluded beach tucked below the cliffs, for a late afternoon swim.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos via the scenic coastal road. Stop in Vila do Bispo for a quick look at the beautiful azulejo-tiled church interior. Arrive back in Lagos for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hostel or café – full Portuguese breakfast with eggs, bread, and coffee (~€7–10)
meals.lunch: Restaurant in Sagres village – grilled tuna steak or percebes (barnacles) with local beer (~€14–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Nah Nah Bah in Lagos – burgers and craft beer for a casual Sunday evening (~€14–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Sagres can be windy even in September – bring a light jacket. The bus from Lagos to Sagres runs regularly but check Sunday schedules. A rental car gives much more flexibility for this day trip. Cabo de São Vicente is free to visit.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge day. Sleep in and enjoy a slow morning at the hostel. Visit the Lagos Municipal Market (Mercado Municipal) for fresh local produce, fish, and regional products. Pick up local almonds, figs, carob, and honey as snacks and souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia da Luz, a charming beach village 6 km west of Lagos (bus or taxi). Enjoy the wide sandy beach backed by dramatic red cliffs. Swim and relax. Explore the small village with its whitewashed houses and local shops. Visit the Roman ruins at the nearby Museu Arqueológico de Lagos if interested in history.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a cooking class or simply dine at a restaurant known for traditional Algarvian cuisine. Explore the nightlife on Rua 25 de Abril for a nightcap.

meals.breakfast: Market breakfast – fresh fruit, local cheese, and bread from the Mercado Municipal (~€6–8)
meals.lunch: Beachside restaurant in Praia da Luz – grilled sardines and salad (~€12–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Dom Sebastião in Lagos – upscale traditional Portuguese cuisine, try the arroz de lingueirão (~€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Lagos Municipal Market is best visited in the morning when it's most lively. Praia da Luz is easily reached by local bus (Eva Transportes). This is a good mid-trip rest day to recharge before the second half of the itinerary.

day_by_day.morning: Book the Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour. Drive or take a tour bus to Benagil (~50 km east of Lagos). Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most beautiful sea caves, accessible only by water. The guided kayak tour takes you through sea arches, hidden grottos, and stunning coastal formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the kayak tour, relax on Praia de Benagil – a tiny beach inside the cove. Explore the surrounding coastline by kayak or on foot along the cliff tops. Visit the nearby Praia de Carvalho, a hidden beach accessible through a tunnel carved in the cliff. Spend the late afternoon unwinding on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Lagos, stopping in Portimão for dinner. Portimão is famous for its grilled sardines – a must-try Algarvian experience.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hostel or a café before departure – toast, coffee, and juice (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Benagil beach – fresh seafood sandwich and cold drink (~€10–14)
meals.dinner: Taberna da Maré in Portimão – famous grilled sardines with boiled potatoes and peppers (~€14–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Benagil Kayak Tour well in advance – it's one of the most popular experiences in the Algarve. Tours typically depart in the morning. The cave can only be entered by kayak, SUP, or small boat – swimming in is not permitted. Wear a swimsuit under your clothes.

day_by_day.morning: Book the Silves Castle & Old Town Food Walk experience. Drive or take the bus to Silves (~35 km northeast of Lagos). Explore the magnificent Moorish red sandstone castle – one of the best-preserved in Portugal. Enjoy panoramic views over the orange groves and Arade River valley from the castle walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the guided food walk through Silves' charming old town. Sample local specialties including medronho (arbutus berry brandy), local cheeses, almond sweets, and traditional pastries. Visit the Silves Cathedral (Sé de Silves), a beautiful Gothic structure built on the site of a former mosque. Browse the artisan shops for handmade ceramics and cork products.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a relaxed evening with dinner at a local restaurant. Share stories from the day over a bottle of Algarve wine.

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagos before departure – coffee and pastel de nata (~€4–6)
meals.lunch: Included in the Silves Food Walk – local tastings and samples throughout the tour
meals.dinner: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves (if staying late) or back in Lagos – seafood rice or grilled fish (~€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Silves is a fascinating historical town often overlooked by tourists – a real hidden gem. The food walk typically lasts 2–3 hours. Silves is easily reached by train from Lagos (change at Tunes) or by car. The castle entrance fee is approximately €3–5.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the western Algarve's wild coast. Drive north from Lagos to the Costa Vicentina Natural Park. Visit Praia de Odeceixe, a stunning river-meets-sea beach straddling the Alentejo border. The dramatic scenery and fewer crowds make it a memorable experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue south along the wild coast to Aljezur. Explore this charming hilltop village with its Moorish castle ruins and whitewashed houses. Visit the local market or artisan shops. Head to Praia da Arrifana, a dramatic surf beach backed by towering cliffs – perfect for watching surfers or trying a beginner surf lesson (~€30–40).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos via the scenic inland route through Monchique foothills. Enjoy dinner back in Lagos.

meals.breakfast: Hostel or café – full breakfast before the day trip (~€7–10)
meals.lunch: Restaurant in Aljezur – try the local sweet potato dishes (batata-doce de Aljezur is a regional specialty) and grilled fish (~€14–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante A Forja in Lagos – traditional Algarvian cuisine in a cozy setting (~€18–24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: A rental car is essential for this day trip as public transport to the wild coast is very limited. The Costa Vicentina is part of a protected natural park – one of the most unspoiled coastlines in Europe. Bring a windbreaker as the Atlantic coast can be breezy.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Monchique, the mountain village in the Serra de Monchique (~45 minutes from Lagos). Drive up through eucalyptus and cork oak forests. Visit the charming village, explore the ruins of the Franciscan convent, and browse local shops selling medronho brandy, honey, and smoked sausages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the summit of Fóia (902m), the highest point in the Algarve, for panoramic views stretching from the Atlantic to the Spanish border on a clear day. Return to Monchique for a relaxing soak at the Caldas de Monchique thermal spa village – a beautiful 19th-century spa resort nestled in a wooded valley. Enjoy the thermal waters or simply stroll through the peaceful gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a final Friday evening in the lively old town. Have dinner at a restaurant with live Fado music if available.

meals.breakfast: Café in Monchique village – local bread, cheese, and coffee (~€6–8)
meals.lunch: Restaurante Central in Monchique – try the famous espetada de porco preto (black pork skewers) with local wine (~€16–22 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Vivant in Lagos – Mediterranean cuisine with a Portuguese twist, great wine list (~€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Monchique is a refreshing change from the coastal heat – temperatures are cooler in the mountains. The thermal spa at Caldas de Monchique offers day passes for the pools (~€15–25). The drive through the mountains is scenic and enjoyable. A car is necessary for this trip.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Praia da Marinha or explore a new beach – Praia de Albandeira or Praia de Benagil area for a final beach morning. Spend time swimming, snorkeling, and soaking up the September sun. Take photos of the stunning coastal scenery to remember the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head back to Lagos for a final afternoon of souvenir shopping and exploration. Visit the Mercado de Lagos for last-minute local products. Pick up cork items, azulejo tiles, local wines, almond sweets, and artisan crafts. Visit any remaining Lagos sights – the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos) or the Municipal Museum.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of Lagos's best restaurants. Splurge slightly on a special meal to celebrate the end of a wonderful trip. Enjoy a final evening stroll along the marina and old town.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or café – leisurely final morning breakfast (~€7–10)
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch – grilled fish and salad at a beachside restaurant (~€14–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Vasco da Gama in Lagos – upscale farewell dinner with fresh seafood and Algarve wines (~€28–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is the last full beach day – make the most of it. September beaches are less crowded than July/August but still warm. Pack souvenirs carefully to avoid breakage. Confirm checkout time with the hostel for the following morning.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Lagos. Wake up early, pack, and check out of Boutique Taghostel. Take one last walk through the Lagos old town and along the seafront. Grab a final pastel de nata and coffee at a local café. Head to Faro Airport by pre-booked taxi or shuttle (~1 hour drive). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days exploring the Algarve's beaches, wines, caves, castles, and coastal landscapes.
day_by_day.evening: In transit home.

meals.breakfast: Final café stop in Lagos – coffee, pastel de nata, and a tosta mista (~€5–8)
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or café at Faro Airport (~€12–18)
meals.dinner: On the plane or at home

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your airport transfer the night before to ensure punctuality. Faro Airport is approximately 70 km from Lagos – allow 60–75 minutes travel time. Check airline baggage allowances if you've purchased wine or other liquid souvenirs. Arrive at the airport at least 2.5 hours before departure.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Boutique Taghostel
hotel.location: Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos, PT (37.1038,-8.6730)

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded cove for a refreshing swim.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most beautiful sea caves, accessible only by water. A guided kayak tour takes you through hidden grottos and arches along the golden coastline, offering a unique perspective of the Algarve's dramatic geology.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience
experiences.description: Visit a local winery in the Lagoa wine region, the heart of Algarve viticulture, for a guided tasting of regional wines including Arinto and Negra Mole varieties. Pair your wines with a traditional Cataplana seafood stew prepared by a local chef.

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat Tour
experiences.description: Cruise through the stunning Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park spanning 60km of coastline. Discover barrier islands, flamingo colonies, and secluded barrier beaches only accessible by boat, with stops for swimming and snorkeling in calm lagoon waters.

experiences.name: Silves Castle & Old Town Food Walk
experiences.description: Explore the Moorish red sandstone castle of Silves, the ancient Algarve capital, followed by a guided food walk through the historic old town. Sample local specialties including carob products, medronho brandy, almond sweets, and fresh orange juice at traditional market stalls.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer pre-arranged to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos (approx. 1 hour drive). Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome glass of local Algarve wine prepared by the hotel. Light room service or a late-night charcuterie board to unwind.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: In-room welcome charcuterie board with local cheeses, cured meats, olives, and a bottle of Algarve white wine arranged by the hotel

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer before departure. Request a late check-in confirmation with the hotel. Ask the hotel concierge to prepare a welcome amenity and next-day breakfast reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late breakfast at the hotel to recover from travel. Afterward, take a gentle orientation stroll through Lagos old town — explore the historic Ponta da Bandeira Fort, the charming cobblestone streets, and the vibrant local market. Stop at a local pastelaria for a mid-morning espresso and pastel de nata.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia Dona Ana, one of Lagos's most iconic golden-sand beaches framed by dramatic ochre cliffs, just a short taxi ride from the hotel. Rent a premium sun lounger and umbrella, swim in the crystal-clear Atlantic, and explore the nearby sea arches and rock formations on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to freshen up. Enjoy a sunset aperitivo on the hotel terrace or rooftop if available. Dinner at a top Lagos restaurant — Restaurante Adega da Marina or Casinha do Petisco — for fresh grilled fish, local cataplana, and a curated selection of Algarve wines.

meals.breakfast: Full Portuguese breakfast at the hotel — fresh bread, local jams, cheese, ham, eggs, fresh orange juice, and espresso
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch at a premium beach club near Praia Dona Ana — grilled prawns, fresh salads, and chilled local rosé
meals.dinner: Fine dining at Restaurante Adega da Marina — whole grilled sea bass, cataplana de marisco, and a bottle of Quinta dos Vales Algarve red

day_by_day.notes: Lagos old town is walkable from the hotel. Praia Dona Ana is approximately 1.5 km from the hotel — a short taxi or tuk-tuk ride. September weather is typically warm and sunny, ideal for beach days.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on the Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim experience. Depart from Lagos by private car (approx. 30 minutes east). Explore one of the Algarve's most breathtaking stretches of coastline — dramatic limestone cliffs, hidden sea caves, natural arches, and turquoise coves. Guided hike along the clifftop trail with stops for swimming in secluded grottos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Marinha coastline or relax on the beach. Enjoy a picnic-style premium lunch prepared by the tour operator or head to a nearby restaurant in Carvoeiro village. In the afternoon, visit the charming village of Carvoeiro — browse boutique shops, enjoy gelato, and admire the scenic beach cove.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by private transfer. Freshen up at the hotel. Dinner at a premium Lagos restaurant — try Bon Vivant or O Camilo for elevated seafood with panoramic Atlantic views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full Portuguese spread with fresh fruit, yogurt, local honey, and pastries
meals.lunch: Alfresco lunch in Carvoeiro village at Restaurante O Castelo — grilled octopus salad, fresh fish of the day, and local white wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at O Camilo Restaurant, perched on the cliffs above Lagos beach — lobster bisque, grilled turbot, and a premium Alentejo wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable hiking shoes and bring swimwear, sunscreen, and a hat for the coastal hike. The trail can be uneven in places. Book the Praia da Marinha experience in advance through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by private car to Benagil (approx. 45 minutes east of Lagos) for the Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour. Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave — one of the world's most photographed sea caves — accessible only by water. The guided tour includes stops at hidden beaches, sea arches, and dramatic coastal formations. A truly unmissable Algarve experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the kayak tour, relax on Praia de Benagil or nearby Praia de Carvalho — two of the Algarve's most beautiful and secluded beaches. Enjoy a leisurely afternoon swim and sunbathing before the private transfer back to Lagos.
day_by_day.evening: Spa evening at the hotel or a nearby luxury spa in Lagos — book a 90-minute massage or body treatment to recover from the active day. Light dinner at a wine bar in Lagos old town.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel — fresh fruit, yogurt, granola, and espresso before departure
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at a local restaurant near Benagil — grilled sardines, fresh bread, tomato salad, and chilled Sagres beer or local rosé
meals.dinner: Intimate dinner at Vinha Bar & Wine in Lagos — premium charcuterie and cheese boards, small plates, and an extensive Algarve and Alentejo wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book the Benagil Kayak Tour well in advance — it is one of the most popular experiences in the Algarve and fills up quickly, especially in September. Wear water shoes and bring a dry bag for valuables.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated wine day — depart by private car to the Lagoa wine region (approx. 40 minutes east) for the Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience. Visit a prestigious local winery such as Quinta dos Vales or Adega do Cantor for a guided vineyard tour, cellar visit, and structured tasting of the region's finest reds, whites, and rosés.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the culinary experience with a traditional Cataplana cooking demonstration and tasting lunch at the winery. The cataplana — a copper clam-shaped pot — is the Algarve's most iconic dish, typically filled with clams, prawns, chorizo, and fresh herbs. Pair with premium Algarve wines. Browse the winery shop for bottles to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos in the late afternoon. Enjoy a relaxed evening — sunset walk along the Lagos marina promenade, cocktails at a rooftop bar, and a lighter dinner to balance the indulgent lunch.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Winery cataplana tasting lunch — traditional cataplana de marisco paired with Quinta dos Vales reserve wines (included in the experience)
meals.dinner: Light dinner at Restaurante Casinha do Petisco in Lagos — tapas-style small plates, local cheeses, and a glass of Algarve sparkling wine

day_by_day.notes: The Algarve Wine & Cataplana Tasting Experience should be booked in advance. Designate a driver or use a private transfer for the wine day — do not drive after tastings. Ask the winery about private reserve tastings for a more exclusive experience.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning for personal leisure. Sleep in, enjoy a long hotel breakfast, and spend time at the hotel pool or terrace. Alternatively, explore Lagos's vibrant Saturday market (Mercado de Lagos) for fresh local produce, artisan crafts, and regional specialties.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat charter from Lagos Marina — a 3-4 hour luxury sailing or motor yacht excursion along the stunning Ponta da Piedade coastline. Explore sea caves, golden arches, and hidden grottos from the water. Swim in secluded coves accessible only by boat. Champagne and snacks served on board.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a clifftop bar overlooking Ponta da Piedade. Dinner at a premium Lagos restaurant — book a table at Restaurante Bon Vivant for contemporary Portuguese cuisine with a modern twist.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast — full spread with fresh pastries, smoked salmon, local cheeses, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: On-board luxury picnic during the boat charter — premium charcuterie, fresh seafood, local cheeses, fruit, and chilled champagne
meals.dinner: Fine dining at Bon Vivant Restaurant Lagos — tasting menu with wine pairing featuring contemporary takes on Portuguese classics

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat charter through the hotel concierge at least 2-3 days in advance. Ponta da Piedade is best experienced from the water — this is one of the highlights of any Algarve trip. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a light layer for the boat.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres — the dramatic southwestern tip of Portugal and continental Europe's most southwesterly point. Depart by private car (approx. 30 minutes west of Lagos). Visit the imposing Fortaleza de Sagres, a 15th-century fortress with sweeping Atlantic views, and the iconic Cabo de São Vicente lighthouse — a truly awe-inspiring landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Sagres village and its pristine, wind-swept beaches — Praia do Martinhal is a premium option with calm waters and a luxury beach club. Enjoy a long, relaxed lunch overlooking the Atlantic. In the afternoon, visit a local surf school for a beginner lesson or simply watch world-class surfers at Praia do Tonel.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a quiet evening — hotel spa, rooftop drinks, and dinner at a local tasca (traditional Portuguese tavern) for an authentic, unpretentious meal.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante A Sagres or Martinhal Beach Club — fresh grilled fish, local clams, and chilled Vinho Verde
meals.dinner: Traditional dinner at Tasca do Celso in Lagos — grilled black pork, local clams with garlic and coriander, and house wine

day_by_day.notes: Sagres can be windy even in September — bring a light jacket. Cabo de São Vicente is one of Portugal's most iconic landmarks and should not be missed. The drive along the coast between Lagos and Sagres is scenic and worth taking slowly.

day_by_day.morning: Depart by private car to Silves (approx. 35 minutes northeast of Lagos) for the Silves Castle & Old Town Food Walk experience. Explore the magnificent Moorish red sandstone castle — one of the best-preserved in Portugal — with panoramic views over the Algarve countryside. A knowledgeable guide provides historical context on the region's Moorish heritage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the guided food walk through Silves old town — sample local specialties including medronho (arbutus berry spirit), local honey, almond sweets, smoked sausages, and artisan cheeses at family-run shops and market stalls. Visit the Silves Municipal Market for a vibrant local experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Sunset drinks at the hotel terrace. Dinner at a premium restaurant — try Restaurante Adega da Marina for a final celebration of Algarve cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Guided food walk lunch in Silves — multiple tastings of local specialties included in the experience, plus a sit-down meal at Restaurante Marisqueira Rui for cataplana and local wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Adega da Marina — whole baked sea bream, clam rice, and a premium Algarve wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Silves is one of the Algarve's most historically rich destinations and often overlooked by tourists — a genuine highlight. The food walk is best enjoyed on an empty stomach. Book the Silves Castle & Old Town Food Walk experience in advance through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed beach morning at Meia Praia — a long, sweeping golden sand beach just east of Lagos, easily accessible by taxi or water taxi from the marina. Rent premium sun loungers at a beach club, swim, and enjoy the calm September waters. Meia Praia is less crowded than the cove beaches and perfect for a leisurely morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos for a premium spa afternoon at the hotel or a nearby luxury wellness center. Book a couples massage, facial, or hydrotherapy treatment. Alternatively, explore Lagos's boutique shopping scene — artisan ceramics, leather goods, local wine, and handmade jewelry.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset catamaran cruise from Lagos Marina — a 2-hour evening sailing experience with wine, canapés, and spectacular golden-hour views of the Ponta da Piedade cliffs. Return to shore for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fresh fruit platter, avocado toast, smoked salmon, and freshly brewed coffee
meals.lunch: Beach club lunch at Meia Praia — grilled tiger prawns, fresh salads, and chilled local rosé
meals.dinner: Late dinner at Restaurante O Camilo — premium seafood tasting menu with Atlantic views and a curated Portuguese wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book the sunset catamaran cruise through the hotel concierge or Lagos Marina directly. September evenings can be slightly cooler on the water — bring a light wrap or jacket. Meia Praia water taxi from Lagos Marina is a fun and scenic way to reach the beach.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ria Formosa Natural Park — depart by private car to Faro (approx. 1 hour east). Board the Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat Tour — a guided cruise through the stunning 60km lagoon system, a UNESCO-protected natural park. Spot flamingos, herons, and migratory birds. Visit barrier islands with pristine, unspoiled beaches accessible only by boat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark on Ilha Deserta (Desert Island) — the most remote and pristine of the Ria Formosa barrier islands. Enjoy a long, peaceful afternoon on one of Portugal's most beautiful and uncrowded beaches. Swim in the warm, sheltered lagoon waters. Lunch at the island's only restaurant — a unique and memorable experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return by boat to Faro. Explore Faro's charming old town — the walled Cidade Velha, the Gothic cathedral, and the atmospheric cobblestone streets. Dinner in Faro before the private transfer back to Lagos.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Estaminé on Ilha Deserta — the only restaurant on the island, serving fresh seafood, clams, and local fish with stunning lagoon views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Faz Gostos in Faro old town — traditional Algarve cuisine with a refined touch, local wines, and a beautiful historic setting

day_by_day.notes: The Ria Formosa boat tour is a full-day commitment — depart Lagos early to maximize time on the island. Book the tour in advance. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and water shoes for the island beaches. The return transfer from Faro to Lagos is approximately 1 hour.

day_by_day.morning: Second wine experience — depart by private car to the Alentejo wine region near Vidigueira or Évora (approx. 2 hours north of Lagos) for a premium winery visit. The Alentejo is Portugal's most celebrated wine region, producing world-class reds. Visit Herdade do Esporão or Herdade dos Grous for an exclusive private tasting and vineyard tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a long winery lunch in the vineyard restaurant — a farm-to-table experience using produce grown on the estate, paired with reserve wines. Browse the winery shop and purchase bottles to take home. Begin the scenic drive back to Lagos through the rolling cork oak and olive tree landscapes of the Alentejo.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Lagos in the early evening. Quiet night at the hotel — room service, a bottle of wine purchased from the winery, and relaxation on the hotel terrace.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Estate restaurant lunch at Herdade do Esporão — seasonal tasting menu with full wine pairing using estate-grown and produced wines
meals.dinner: In-room dinner — premium room service or a curated hotel cheese and charcuterie board with a bottle of Alentejo red from the winery visit

day_by_day.notes: The Alentejo day trip is a longer drive but absolutely worthwhile for wine enthusiasts. Arrange a private driver for the full day. Herdade do Esporão requires advance reservation for private tastings and restaurant lunch. This is one of Portugal's finest wine estates.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — return to Praia da Marinha or discover Praia do Camilo, a hidden gem near Lagos accessible via a wooden staircase down the cliffs. Spend the morning swimming, snorkeling, and soaking in the Algarve's extraordinary coastal scenery one last time. Rent premium equipment for snorkeling to explore the underwater rock formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos for a farewell afternoon — visit any remaining boutiques or artisan shops for last-minute gifts and souvenirs. Enjoy a final spa treatment at the hotel. Pack and prepare for departure the following day. Afternoon tea or cocktails at the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — the finest meal of the trip. Book a table at a premium Lagos restaurant or arrange a private chef dinner experience through the hotel. Celebrate the journey with a multi-course tasting menu, premium wine pairing, and a toast to Portugal.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast — full spread, fresh pastries, and a final espresso on the terrace
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at a premium beach club — grilled lobster, fresh salads, and a bottle of chilled Algarve white wine
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at Bon Vivant Restaurant Lagos — full tasting menu with premium wine pairing, finishing with local medronho digestif and petits fours

day_by_day.notes: Consider arranging a private chef dinner at the hotel for an ultra-exclusive farewell experience — speak to the concierge at least 3 days in advance. Purchase any remaining wine, ceramics, or local products before departure. Confirm departure transfer for the following day.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Lagos — enjoy a last leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Take a slow farewell walk through Lagos old town, stop for a final espresso and pastel de nata at a local café, and soak in the atmosphere of this beautiful Algarve town one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel. Private luxury transfer to Faro Airport for departure. Arrive at the airport with ample time for check-in and security. Browse the airport shops for any final Portuguese wine, port, or specialty food purchases.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days in the Algarve — world-class beaches, exceptional wines, historic culture, and unforgettable coastal scenery.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — full Portuguese spread with fresh fruit, pastries, local cheeses, and espresso
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hotel or a nearby café before departure — soup, sandwich, and fresh juice
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for the Faro Airport transfer and check-in process. Confirm the private transfer booking the evening before. Faro Airport has a good selection of Portuguese wine and specialty food shops for last-minute purchases. Obrigado e boa viagem — thank you and safe travels!
